//: editorconfig-checker — enforces .editorconfig, which nothing else in this repo reads.
What it flags: a Java line ending in a space (trim_trailing_whitespace) or a file with
no closing newline (insert_final_newline) — and a body indented '  return x;' when
[*.{java,xml}] pins indent_size=4, so it demands '    return x;' instead.
Indentation checks are ON. The excludes below fall into two groups.
Generated artifacts: regenerating them would just reintroduce the violation.
Embedded-content files: every remaining violation in these sits inside a string
literal — Java text blocks holding JSON fixtures and LLM prompts, and Python triple-
quoted strings holding HTML/CSS templates. Those lines are DATA, not code indentation,
and the checker cannot tell the difference. Re-indenting them to fit the grid would
change the literal string: ApiExamples feeds openapi.yaml (a committed, drift-checked
artifact), two are prompts sent to a model, and the Python ones are generated web pages.
